title: What is the difference between Object and Objects?
shortTitle: What is the difference between Object and Objects?
keyPoints: Object (java.lang.Object): the root class, parent of every Java class
Objects (java.util.Objects): a utility class with static helper methods (since Java 7)
Objects.hash(fields...): convenient multi-field hash code generation
Objects.requireNonNull(x, msg): throws NPE with a clear message if x is null

s1_definition.oneliner: Object is the root class of all Java classes. Objects (java.util.Objects) is a utility class with null-safe static helpers: equals, hash, requireNonNull, toString.
s1_definition.profdef:
Two different things:

- **Object** (java.lang.Object): The root class. Every class extends it. Provides instance methods: toString, equals, hashCode.
- **Objects** (java.util.Objects): A utility class since Java 7. Provides static helper methods for null-safe operations.
s1_definition.analogy: Object is the bank template form. Objects is the office toolbox with null-safe stamps, validators, and comparison tools.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Object (java.lang.Object):     root class, parent of all
  Objects (java.util.Objects):    utility class, static helpers

  Objects.equals(a, b)        → null-safe equality
  Objects.hash(f1, f2, ...)   → multi-field hashCode
  Objects.requireNonNull(x)   → NPE with message if null
  Objects.toString(x, "N/A")  → null-safe toString
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Object is the root class of all Java classes. Objects is a utility class with null-safe static helpers. Use Objects.equals() for null-safe comparison, Objects.hash() for multi-field hash codes, and Objects.requireNonNull() for parameter validation.

One sentence to remember: Object is the parent class, Objects is the utility toolbox – use Objects.equals for null-safe comparison and Objects.hash for hash codes.
